reasoning.1: Q is orthogonal (Q^T Q = I) but det Q = -1, so it is not a rotation. Computing Q^T A Q gives diag(-2, 4, 6), a diagonal matrix.
reasoning.2: A is symmetric with eigenvalues 1 and 3, so (A-I)(A-3I)=0 and A^2 = 4A - 3I.
reasoning.3: det A = 1*2 - 2*3 = -4, so A is non-singular and (B) is false. Eigenvalues are 4 and -1, distinct and real, so A is diagonalizable. A^T A != I kills (D).
reasoning.4: Direct computation: A^3 - A^2 - A + I3 is the zero matrix, i.e. the null matrix.
reasoning.5: Expanding the determinant in the last row with the stated cofactors B, C, F of b, c, f gives Delta*a = BC - F^2, so (BC - F^2)/a = Delta.
reasoning.6: The determinant reduces to -4a^2b^2c^2 in this arrangement, so K = 4.
reasoning.7: cos(3pi/5) < 0, so z = sec(3pi/5) e^{i3pi/5} has |z| = |sec| = -sec(3pi/5) and arg = 3pi/5 - pi = -2pi/5.
reasoning.8: The official page states i z^3 + z^2 - z + i = 0. All three roots have modulus 1.
reasoning.9: e = c/a = 3/2, which is option (C). An earlier draft recorded (A) - wrong option letter.
reasoning.10: With vertex A at the origin, the focal-chord relations give Delta = a^2(t+1/t)^2/2, and the ordinate difference is 2a(t+1/t); eliminating t yields 2Delta/a.
reasoning.11: Completing the square gives centre (sqrt2,-sqrt2) with a=2sqrt3, b=sqrt6, c=3sqrt2. With A the vertex nearer the focus and B an end of the latus rectum, the area is sqrt(3/2) - 1.
reasoning.13: Work = F.AB = 6, which is option (B). An earlier draft recorded (A) = sqrt6 - wrong letter.
reasoning.14: h = f^2 + (f')^2 and h' = 2f f' + 2f' f'' = 2f f' - 2f' f = 0, so h is constant and h(10) = h(5) = 11.
reasoning.15: x = 1 satisfies 10+5 = 8+7 = 15, so there is a non-zero integral solution. (B) is false for the same reason and (D) fails at x = 2.
reasoning.16: Logarithm: (1/x)ln(e^x+x), and ln(1+2x+O(x^2)) = 2x+O(x^2), so the log tends to 2 and the limit is e^2.
reasoning.17: Both solvers agree under the strict reading: f(a)=f(b) with a<b forces 0 into the open interval, where |x| is not differentiable, so Rolle never applies. (D).
reasoning.18: Chord AB joins (-1,-1) and (2,8): slope 3. Setting 3x^2 = 3 gives x = +1 and x = -1, and BOTH are points of the curve carrying tangent slope 3 - indeed the tangent at A is y = 3x + 2, which passes through B, so the chord IS the tangent at A. Two points, option (C).
reasoning.19: The opposite corner lies on x/a + y/b = 1 and the area xy peaks at x=a/2, y=b/2 - the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
reasoning.20: With P=(at^2,2at) the tangent meets the directrix at K=(-a,a(t^2-1)/t), and (F-K).(F-P) = 0 identically, so KP subtends 90 degrees at the focus.
reasoning.21: Similar triangles: s/x = 2/(6-2), so s = x/2 and ds/dt = v/2 = 3 km/h.
reasoning.22: u_x = 1/a - b f', u_y = a f', so a u_x + b u_y = 1 + f'(-ab + ab) = 1.
reasoning.23: v_x = x/(r sqrt(1-r^2)) and v_y = y/(r sqrt(1-r^2)) with r^2 = x^2+y^2, so x v_x + y v_y = r/sqrt(1-r^2) = tan v.
reasoning.24: Differentiating ((x^n+1)/x^n)^((n-1)/n) reproduces the integrand only with the factor -1/(n-1).
reasoning.26: Differentiating 2(sqrt x - 1)/sqrt(1-x) reproduces the integrand exactly, so this is the antiderivative.
reasoning.27: dy/dx = y/x - cos^2(y/x) is homogeneous. With v=y/x: x v' = -cos^2 v, so -sec^2 v dv = dx/x and -tan v = ln x + c. At (1, pi/4): tan v = 1 - ln x, i.e. x = e^{1-tan(y/x)}, which is printed as option (B). Three passes now agree on (B); our first draft computed this correctly and then keyed (A).
reasoning.28: Roots -1,-1 give (A+Bx)e^{-x}; substituting y = a e^{2x} gives 9a = 2, so the particular integral is (2/9)e^{2x}.
reasoning.29: Divisible by 36 needs divisibility by 4 and 9. The digit sum 45 is always a multiple of 9, so only the last two digits matter: 16 favourable ordered pairs out of 72.
reasoning.30: P(A')+P(B') = 2 - [P(A)+P(B)] and P(A)+P(B) = P(AuB)+P(AnB) = 0.9, so the sum is 1.1.
reasoning.31: det A = lambda(lambda-2)(lambda+1). Rank is 2 at lambda = 0, 2, -1 and 3 otherwise. Option (B) is printed as '3 for lambda != 0, 2, -1' - the != IS printed - so (B) is true as well as (A). (C) and (D) are false.
reasoning.32: The circulant determinant is (a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca) = half(a+b+c)[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2], which vanishes iff a+b+c = 0 or a = b = c. Both (A) and (B) therefore give non-zero solutions.
reasoning.33: From 2cos t = x + 1/x we get x = e^{i t}. Then x/y + y/x = 2cos(t-u) and xy + 1/(xy) = 2cos(t+u), so (A) and (C) are identically true and (B), (D) are not.
reasoning.34: The latus rectum subtending a right angle at the centre gives e^4 - 3e^2 + 1 = 0, so e^2 = (3+sqrt5)/2 and e = (sqrt5+1)/2, which is also less than 2.
reasoning.35: a x (b x c) = (a.c)b - (a.b)c, a combination of b and c, so it is coplanar with b and c (B) and perpendicular to a (C). It is not coplanar with a and b (A) and not perpendicular to c (D).
reasoning.36: Split on the sign of y. For y>=0: x + y = 2y gives y = x, valid only for x>=0. For y<0: x - y = 2y gives y = x/3, valid only for x<0. So y = x on [0,inf) and y = x/3 on (-inf,0). Every real x has exactly one y (A true); both branches tend to 0 (B true); the slopes are 1 and 1/3 so it is not differentiable at 0 (C false); the slope for x<0 is 1/3 (D true).
reasoning.37: Tangents of slope m to x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 are y = mx +- sqrt(a^2 m^2 + b^2). With a^2 = 16, b^2 = 9 and m = 1 the intercepts are +-5, i.e. y = x + 5 and y = x - 5.
reasoning.38: |xy^2 + x^2y|/(x^2+y^2) <= |xy|(|x|+|y|)/(x^2+y^2) <= (|x|+|y|)/2, which tends to 0, so f is continuous at the origin (C true). Both partials vanish because f(h,0) = f(0,h) = 0 for every h, so fx(0,0) = fy(0,0) = 0 (D true) and (A), (B) are false.
reasoning.39: sqrt2 arcsin u and -sqrt2 arccos u differ by a constant, so both are valid antiderivatives. (A) and (B) are both correct.
reasoning.40: x dy = y(dx + y dy) rearranges to x dy - y dx = y^2 dy, so d(x/y) = -dy and x/y = C - y. With y(1)=1: C=2, hence x = 2y - y^2. At x = -3 this gives y^2 - 2y - 3 = 0, so y = 3 or y = -1 - both (A) and (C). This is a Category-II item (page 9 header: Q31-40, one or more options correct), so two answers are allowed. Earlier drafts called this a defect on the strength of a wrong solution x = y(1-ln y); that came from mis-integrating the equation.
reasoning.41: The phase (p/v - qpi) must be dimensionless: p/v has dimension T, so p is a length; qpi is dimensionless, so q is a time.
reasoning.42: dV/V = dL/L + dh/h + dt/t = 0.01 + 0.01 + 0.01 = 0.03, and V = 1.0 cm^3, so the error is 0.03 cm^3.
reasoning.43: (Q-P) x (R-P) = (-5,1,-9) with magnitude sqrt107, so the area is sqrt107/2.
reasoning.44: F_rad = 2 alpha x / R, proportional to x, which is option (A). An earlier draft's reasoning reached 'proportional to x' but recorded (D).
reasoning.45: y = x tan t - g x^2/(2u^2 cos^2 t). Comparing with 2x - 5x^2 gives tan t = 2 and g/(2u^2cos^2t) = 5; with g = 10 and cos^2t = 1/5 we get u^2 = 5, so u = sqrt5 and the components are (1, 2).
reasoning.46: The block oscillates about the new equilibrium x0 = F/k with amplitude F/k, and F/k = F/(m omega^2).
reasoning.47: Work done against friction = integral from 10 to 100 of (k/x) dx = k ln10 = 0.5*2.3 = 1.15 J, so KE = 2 - 1.15 = 0.85 J.
reasoning.49: V(x) = -2Gm/sqrt(x^2+a^2), so |V| peaks at x=0 and falls to zero as x grows - a bell shape.
reasoning.50: For a longitudinal stress, dV/V = (dL/L)(1 - 2 sigma). Here dL/L = +0.01 and dV/V = +0.004, so 1 - 2 sigma = 0.4 and sigma = 0.3.
reasoning.51: Equal flow rates: L^2 sqrt(2gy) = pi R^2 sqrt(2g(2y)) = pi R^2 sqrt2 sqrt(2gy), so R/L = 1/(2^{1/4} sqrt pi).
reasoning.52: At terminal velocity the weight is balanced by buoyancy plus 6 pi eta R v, and heat rate = 6 pi eta R v^2 proportional to R * R^2 = R^5.
reasoning.53: With gamma = 0 the conductivity is constant beta, so the flux is S beta (T1-T2)/L.
reasoning.54: The empty volume stays constant, so the glass and mercury expand equally: 1000 * 2.7e-5 = V * 1.8e-4 gives V = 150 cm^3.
reasoning.55: Isobaric: W = nR dT and Q = nCp dT, so W/Q = R/Cp = 2/5 for a monatomic gas.
reasoning.56: mu = cot(A/2) gives sin((A+dm)/2) = cos(A/2), so (A+dm)/2 = 90 - A/2 and dm = 180 - 2A. Then cos dm = -cos 2A, option (C).
reasoning.57: Image depth is x/mu, so d = (H-x) + x/mu. Then d(H) = H/mu and d(0) = H - a straight line falling from H to H/mu.
reasoning.58: The bright disc has radius r = sqrt(200/pi) = 7.979 cm, so tan c = r/h = 1.1398 and sin c = 0.7517. With sin c = 1/mu, mu = 1.330 and mu^2 = 1.77.
reasoning.59: Lens: 1/f = (1.5-1)(2/10) = 0.1, so f = 10 cm. The liquid fills the gap between the lens and the plane mirror, forming a plano-concave lens of radius 10 cm: P_liq = (mu-1)(1/(-10) - 0) = (1-mu)/10. Combination: 1/F = 1/10 + (1-mu)/10 = (2-mu)/10. Setting F = 25 cm gives 2-mu = 0.4, so mu = 1.6, which is option (C) exactly. No option is reachable by any other reading - 1.6 is the only value that reproduces the printed 25 cm.
reasoning.60: A 5000 A photon carries 1.243*2 = 2.486 eV, and with a 1.36 V stopping potential the work function is 2.486 - 1.36 = 1.126 eV, which is option (D) 1.12 eV.
reasoning.61: Momentum requires v' = 6/(2cos30) = 2sqrt3, so both printed speed options (sqrt3) are false. KE falls from 18m to 12m, so the only true statement is (C).
reasoning.62: In the V-T diagram the vertical axis is V: C-to-A is vertical (T constant) = isothermal, B-to-C is horizontal (V constant) = isochoric, and A-to-B is a straight line through the origin = isobaric. On a P-V diagram that is: horizontal isobar A-to-B, vertical isochore B-to-C, hyperbolic isotherm C-to-A. Only panel (C) has exactly these three shapes; panel (D) draws the isotherm as a straight line and panel (A) as a curve.
reasoning.63: The displaced liquid mass is fixed, and the melt volume is m/rho_w. If rho_L > rho_w the displaced volume was smaller than the melt water, so the level rises.
reasoning.64: Equal density planets have v_esc proportional to R. Mp < Mq means Vp < Vq, and W with mass Mp+Mq has the largest radius, so Vp < Vq < Vw.
reasoning.65: Free expansion is alpha L dT = 1e-4*1000*30 = 3 mm, but only 1 mm of gap exists, so the restrained strain is 2/1000 and the stress is Y*strain = 2e8 Pa.
reasoning.66: Mixed Cv = 2R gives gamma = 3/2 (A true). Energy per mole is 2RT, so (B) as printed is the same statement and is true. The mixture has 4 degrees of freedom, not 5, so (C) is false. rms ratio He:H2 = sqrt(2/4) = 1:sqrt2 (D true).
reasoning.67: Work from 0 to d vanishes: A d - B d^2/2 = 0 gives d = 2A/B (A true). At x = d the acceleration is (A - B*2A/B)/m = -A/m (B true). The acceleration opposes displacement and is not constant, so (C) and (D) are false.
reasoning.68: Equal final speeds with equal masses force v = v0/2 by momentum (A true). Energy then gives omega = sqrt6 v0/L (B true). Angular momentum about the CM is conserved, so (C) is false. That omega with L = h gives h = L/sqrt6 (D true).
reasoning.69: Lens (f=15) with object at 30 cm: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 gives I1 30 cm behind the lens, i.e. 20 cm behind the mirror - a virtual object for the mirror, so (C) is true. The mirror returns I2 20 cm in front of itself, i.e. 10 cm left of the lens, so (A) is true. That converging light meets the lens first, so I2 is a VIRTUAL object for the second lens pass: 1/v = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6 gives the final image 6 cm left of the lens, i.e. 16 cm from the mirror - so (B) is true and (D) is true, since the light actually converges there. The printed 16 cm confirms this reading: 16 = 6 + 10 is reachable only via the virtual-object pass.
reasoning.70: Equal intensity means equal photon flux in energy terms, so the lower-frequency (blue) light delivers more photons per second and ejects more electrons. Violet photons each carry more energy, so their maximum KE is higher, killing (C). Work function is a material property, killing (D). Frequency order makes (A) false.
reasoning.71: Moles reacting are x M1 / 2 = y M2 / 3, so 3 x M1 = 2 y M2.
reasoning.72: Molality = moles solute per kg solvent. In 1 L, solvent mass is 1000 z - x y grams, and molality = x / ((1000z - xy)/1000) = 1000x/(1000z - xy).
reasoning.73: de Broglie: lambda = h/p and p = sqrt(2meV), so lambda = h/sqrt(2meV).
reasoning.74: Cu is [Ar]3d10 4s1; Cu+ loses the 4s electron, leaving [Ar]3d10.
reasoning.75: Equivalent conductivity is molar conductivity divided by the total charge of the ions per formula unit, v+ z+.
reasoning.76: At equal concentration, alpha = sqrt(Ka/c) for each acid, so alpha/alpha' = sqrt(Ka/Ka').
reasoning.77: Bohr's model needs exactly one electron. Li2+ has one (Z=3, two removed). H+ and He2+ have ZERO electrons and Li+ has two, so (C) is the only correct choice.
reasoning.78: Zn(OH)2 is amphoteric and also dissolves in excess ammonia by forming the tetraammine complex. Al(OH)3 dissolves in KOH but not in ammonia, so the 'both' condition selects zinc.
reasoning.80: Acid strength rises with the number of terminal oxygens: HClO4 > HClO3 > HClO2 > HClO.
reasoning.81: NH3 has three bond pairs and one lone pair, so the electron geometry is tetrahedral and the molecular shape is pyramidal.
reasoning.82: C4H9Cl has four structural isomers: 1-chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane, 1-chloro-2-methylpropane and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.
reasoning.83: Zinc oxide is the white pigment used in paints; the other three are coloured.
reasoning.85: Lithium is the only alkali metal that combines directly with nitrogen, forming Li3N.
reasoning.86: BaCl2 and RbCl are salts of strong acids and strong bases, so their solutions are neutral. AlCl3 and BeCl2 hydrolyse to acidic solutions.
reasoning.87: Oxidation-state changes: P from +5 to -3 is 8; N from +5 to 0 is 5; S from +6 to 0 is 6; borax to diborane is not redox. The largest change is phosphorus.
reasoning.88: Spontaneity needs dG = dH - T dS < 0. With both negative and |dH| > |T dS|, dG < 0 (A true). With both positive and |dH| < |T dS|, dG < 0 (B true). Equality gives equilibrium, and case (D) gives dG > 0.
reasoning.89: For an exothermic reaction Kp falls as T rises, so it rises as T falls (C true). For an endothermic reaction Kp falls as T falls (D true). (A) and (B) state the opposite of van't Hoff.
reasoning.90: CaCO3 contains covalent C-O bonds inside the carbonate ion, so (D) is also true alongside H2O and CH4. Only NaCl is purely ionic.
reasoning.91: A moving-iron instrument responds to the RMS value, which for a sinusoid is Vm/sqrt2.
reasoning.92: Referred to the primary, Z2' = Z2 (N1/N2)^2 = (0.5+j0.8)*100 = 50+j80, and the total is Z1 + Z2' = 52+j85 ohm.
reasoning.93: Slip s = 1 - N/Ns exceeds 1 only when N < 0. In the figure W is the point to the LEFT of the vertical axis, so W is (A); Z is at N > Ns (negative slip).
reasoning.94: v = 200 cos(2000t - 40 deg) and i = 4 cos(2000t + 11.32 deg), so the voltage lags the current by 51.32 degrees - a capacitive circuit, hence resistance and capacitance.
reasoning.95: In series the current is common and P = I^2 R, so the higher-resistance 40 W lamp dissipates more and glows brighter.
reasoning.96: The diode blocks the positive half-cycle, so the output is the negative half-wave whose average is -Vm/pi.
reasoning.97: The comparator switches when vi crosses the 3 V reference. With peak 6 V, sin t > 0.5 over the 30 to 150 degree range, i.e. 120 degrees of conduction.
reasoning.98: From the drawing: A in series, then the parallel pair [upper (B+C) || lower ((D+E) then F)], then G. So Y = A[(B+C) + F(D+E)]G, option (C).
reasoning.99: Vcc = Vcb + Ic Rc = 3 + 15 mA * 100 ohm = 3 + 1.5 = 4.5 V.
reasoning.100: An open-circuited shunt field leaves only residual flux, so starting torque (proportional to flux) is negligible and the motor fails to pick up speed, while the armature draws a very large current because there is no back EMF. The question says the motor is STARTED - the racing behaviour belongs to a motor already running whose field opens, which is a different case.
